Su24.name: Su-24M Fencer
Su24.description: Soviet-era variable-sweep wing strike aircraft. Primary Russian tactical bomber, extensively used in Syria and Ukraine. Being gradually replaced by Su-34 but still widely deployed.

Su25.name: Su-25 Grach
Su25.description: Russia's equivalent to the A-10. Heavily armored close air support aircraft designed for low-altitude battlefield interdiction. Titanium cockpit bathtub protects pilot. Heavy losses in Ukraine due to MANPADS threats.

Su34.name: Su-34 Fullback
Su34.description: Modern strike fighter replacing the Su-24. Distinctive flat nose with side-by-side cockpit. Can perform both air-to-ground and air-to-air missions. Russia's primary precision strike platform in Ukraine. Approximately 150 in service.

Su57.name: Su-57 Felon
Su57.description: Russia's 5th generation stealth fighter. Only ~10 delivered to Russian Air Force. Features internal weapons bays, supercruise capability, and advanced avionics. Limited combat use in Ukraine for standoff missile launches.

Mig29.name: MiG-29 Fulcrum
Mig29.description: Lightweight air superiority fighter designed to counter the F-16. Exceptional maneuverability with helmet-mounted sight. Widely exported. MiG-29SMT variant still in Russian service with upgraded radar and avionics.

Mig31.name: MiG-31 Foxhound
Mig31.description: World's fastest combat aircraft in service. Designed to intercept cruise missiles and high-altitude bombers across Russia's vast territory. MiG-31K variant is the carrier platform for the Kinzhal hypersonic missile. Four aircraft can control 800km of airspace.

Tu95.name: Tu-95MS Bear
weapons: Kh-101/102 stealth cruise missile (8 external + 6 internal)
Tu95.description: Iconic Soviet strategic bomber with contra-rotating turboprops. Loudest aircraft ever built. Despite 1950s design, remains Russia's primary cruise missile carrier. Regularly launches Kh-101 strikes against Ukraine from standoff range over the Caspian Sea. ~60 in service.

Tu160.name: Tu-160 White Swan
Tu160.description: Largest and heaviest combat aircraft ever built. Variable-sweep supersonic strategic bomber. Russia's most capable nuclear delivery platform. Only ~17 in service, based at Engels-2. Tu-160M2 modernized variant in production. Regularly used to launch cruise missiles at Ukraine.

Tu22M.name: Tu-22M3 Backfire
Tu22M.description: Variable-sweep supersonic bomber designed for maritime strike against carrier groups. Used extensively for carpet bombing in Syria and Ukraine with unguided FAB bombs. Tu-22M3M modernized variant carries precision-guided munitions. ~60 in service.

Il76.name: Il-76 Candid
Il76.description: Soviet heavy transport workhorse. Can carry tanks, troops, and heavy equipment. Also serves as aerial refueling tanker (Il-78), AWACS (A-50), and laser lab (A-60). Critical for Russian power projection. High activity indicates troop/equipment movements.

Ka52.name: Ka-52 Alligator
Ka52.description: Russia's most advanced attack helicopter with coaxial rotors (no tail rotor). Side-by-side cockpit with ejection seats — unique for helicopters. Extensive combat use in Ukraine for anti-armor operations. Features FLIR, laser designator, and millimeter-wave radar.

Mi8.name: Mi-8/Mi-17 Hip
Mi8.description: Most produced helicopter in aviation history (17,000+). The backbone of Russian rotary-wing operations — troop transport, medevac, cargo, VIP. Mi-8AMTSh armed variant used for assault missions. Presence indicates active military operations at a base.

Mi24.name: Mi-24 Hind
Mi24.description: Iconic Soviet attack helicopter — the 'flying tank'. Unique design combines firepower with troop-carrying cabin. Can deliver 8 soldiers while providing fire support. Battle-proven in Afghanistan, Chechnya, Syria, and Ukraine.

Mi28.name: Mi-28N Night Hunter
Mi28.description: Russia's dedicated attack helicopter, equivalent to the AH-64 Apache. Night-capable with FLIR and radar. Mi-28NM upgraded variant features millimeter-wave radar above rotor hub. Active in Ukraine for anti-armor strikes.

An124.name: An-124 Ruslan
An124.description: One of the largest aircraft in the world. Can carry main battle tanks, S-400 missile systems, or entire helicopter units. Critical for rapid strategic deployment. Only ~10 in Russian military service. Presence at a base signals major equipment movement.

An22.name: An-22 Antei
An22.description: World's largest turboprop-powered aircraft. Soviet-era heavy lifter capable of operating from unprepared airstrips. Very few remain in service. Sighting indicates heavy logistics operations.

fighter.name: Unidentified Fighter
fighter.description: Fighter-class aircraft detected but specific type not classified. Could be Su-27/30/35 family, MiG-29, or similar. Requires higher-resolution imagery or Stage 2 classifier for identification.

bomber.name: Unidentified Bomber
bomber.description: Bomber-class aircraft detected. Could be Tu-22M3, Tu-95MS, Tu-160, or Su-24. Large airframe visible on apron.

transport.name: Unidentified Transport
transport.description: Transport-class aircraft detected. Could be Il-76, An-124, C-130, or similar. Presence indicates logistics activity.
